question: Does heart-driven collective cell-volume response survive unequal spoke stiffnesses and shell inertias?
assumptions: Same chosen scalar/radial model and unsigned determinant-volume readout; no native carrier amplitude identification.
Kh=Ks=Ih=1,Kt=1/2; each positive spoke g_i and shell inertia m_i varied.
Pulse a0=1/10, all shell coordinates and all velocities0; no forcing/damping in pulse scan.
Harmonic shape calculation is a separate small-signal experiment, with unit heart amplitude for ratios; absolute amplitudes may be rescaled.
Time u and parameters remain model-unit quantities; physical/native/material calibration OPEN.
physical_mapping: ASSUMED radial strain/geometry and energy law; readout is unsigned cell volume. Physical clock, material and native variables OPEN.
target_exposure: Previous illustrative spectrum lambda1,4,6 and heart-breathing target exposed. No empirical numeric data.

fitted_choices.target: retain uniform shape at the already exposed reference lambda6
fitted_choices.scope: one engineered mode; does not preserve both original collective modes

historical source/clock/constitutive distinction; no native coefficients imported

result: EXACT/CONDITIONAL: positive-energy stability survives all positive spoke/inertia perturbations, but all-frequency coherence fails near a former differential mode. NUMERICAL: among256 corners per variation level over u0..100, max RMS differential volume-signal fractions are1.88%,9.35%,21.25%,40.68% for ±1%,±5%,±10%,±20%. Exact shape identity explains reinforcement/cancellation; in-phase mode is protected when onsite stiffness/inertia ratios match.
limitations: Finite1280 numerical probes and specified windows do not exhaust the continuous parameter box or all times.
